audit.whatIsWrong: Fate Sealed is called a knock-up twice — 'don't get caught flat-footed by his R knock-up mid-blink, since that point-and-click lockdown' (late) and 'dash back in with R to knock you up' (wants.foe[2]). It is also described as a 'dash-through' in spikes[1] and whys[3].
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Yone blinks behind the last champion in a line with a slash so powerful it pulls all enemies hit towards him.' It is a pull, not a knock-up, and it is not point-and-click — it is a line that targets the LAST champion in it, 1000 range, 120/100/80 seconds. Every part of that changes your positioning. It pulls you toward him rather than throwing you up, so tenacity-style thinking and knockup-dependent reads are the wrong frame; and because it anchors on the last champion in the line, standing at the BACK of your group is what makes you the target. A Kassadin who is told this is a point-and-click knockup will position exactly wrong in every teamfight.
audit.corrected: Fate Sealed: 120s at rank 1, 1000 range. It blinks him behind the LAST champion in the line and pulls everyone it hit toward him — so do not be the deepest body in a line.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yone.json (R description, cooldown 120/100/80, range 1000, dash flag only)

audit.whatIsWrong: Soul Unbound is framed as his escape — 'before his E snaps his spirit back to his body and escapes', 'before his E returns his spirit to safety', 'before his E escape triggers'.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Yone's spirit leaves his body behind, gaining Move Speed. When this ability ends, Yone's spirit is forced back to his body and he repeats a portion of the damage he dealt as a spirit.' Forced is the operative word — he does not choose where he lands, he lands on the body he already left. That inverts the counterplay the page teaches. Instead of racing to kill him before he escapes, you hold the ground where the body is standing, and his exit delivers him back into your burst. It is also a damage amplifier, not a disengage: the portion he repeats on return is why the trade hurts more than it looked. 22s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Soul Unbound (22s at rank 1) is a commitment, not an escape — his spirit is FORCED back to the body he left behind. Stand on the body and his exit is a return trip into you.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'I save Null Sphere's shield and channel-interrupt for when he commits his Q3' (early), repeated as 'Hold Null Sphere's shield and channel-interrupt to blank his Q3 knock-up' (wants.you[1]).
audit.why: Null Sphere interrupts channels. The two-stack Mortal Steel is a dash with a knockup — 'At 2 stacks, Mortal Steel dashes Yone forward with a gust of wind knocking enemies Airborne' — not a channel, so there is nothing for the interrupt to catch. The shield half is real and worth holding; the interrupt half is a button the reader will press at the worst possible moment expecting a cancel that never happens.
audit.corrected: Hold the Null Sphere shield for the Q3 hit. There is no channel in Mortal Steel for the interrupt to catch.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yone.json (Q description, dash + knockup flags, no channel)

audit.whatIsWrong: Spirit Cleave is described as generic 'cleave poke' with no range, no cooldown and no mention of the shield scaling.
audit.why: It is 700 range on 14 seconds, and Riot's text says it 'Grants a shield to Yone, the value is increased by the number of champions hit by the swipe'. Seven hundred out-ranges your 650 Null Sphere, which is the actual reason you lose the pre-6 poke war and the reason 'last-hit at max Null Sphere range' is not as safe as the page implies. The shield also means a Spirit Cleave thrown just before your blink-in blunts the burst you were counting on. Its cooldown scales with attack speed, so 14s is the ceiling, not the floor.
audit.corrected: Spirit Cleave is 700 range on 14s — it out-reaches your 650 Null Sphere and shields him per champion clipped, and its cooldown shortens as he builds attack speed.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yone.json (W description, cooldown 14, range 700, shield flag)

audit.why: Sides and ratings untouched. Yone owning 1-5 with free-cost abilities and a 700-range shielded cleave, Skill at 6, and the item stages contested is consistent, and the content whys already tell the same story in the same order. 57.50% over 40 games is a healthy sample but a whole-game figure.
Null Sphere interrupts channels and grants a magic-absorbing shield; it has never silenced in this kit version.
audit.corrected: Null Sphere interrupts channels; it does not silence.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither Soul Unbound (named as the matchup-defining cooldown) nor Fate Sealed carries a number anywhere on the page.
audit.why: Soul Unbound is 22/19/16/13/10 and Fate Sealed is 120/100/80. The gap between them is the whole commit schedule: his skirmish tool comes back three times before his teamfight tool does, so 'is Soul Unbound down' is the wrong single question the winCon row asks — a spent Fate Sealed is worth far more to you than a spent Soul Unbound.
audit.corrected: Soul Unbound 22s at rank 1; Fate Sealed 120s at rank 1. Commit off the ultimate, not off the spirit.

audit.why: 57.50% over 40 games. The page quotes no figure. No change.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are the worst of this lane for me — Yone's Q dash plus W Spirit Cleave (shield then cleave) out-trades me hard and I have no Riftwalk to escape, so I just last-hit at max Null Sphere range and refuse every all-in. I save Null Sphere's shield and channel-interrupt for when he commits his Q3 (the third cast, the knock-up), then immediately walk out rather than trading autos back. My mana is too thin before Nether Blade restores on champion hits, so I concede the wave and farm.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are the worst of this lane for you — Mortal Steel plus Spirit Cleave out-trade you hard and you have no Riftwalk to escape, so last-hit at max Null Sphere range and refuse every all-in. Spirit Cleave is 700 range against your 650 and shields him for every champion it clips, so you lose the poke war too. Hold the Null Sphere shield for his Q3 knock-up, then walk rather than trading autos. Concede the wave until Nether Blade restores on champion hits.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are still a weather-the-storm window — a maxed Null Sphere plus Nether Blade's champion-hit mana restore let me survive his W cleave poke and farm under tower, but I'm not fighting him yet. At 6 Riftwalk changes everything: I finally have a blink to dodge his Q3 knock-up and his R dash-through, so he can't just collapse on me, and I can blink out the instant his combo whiffs. This is the stage I climb from losing to even and start tipping it my way.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are still a weather-the-storm window — a maxed Null Sphere plus Nether Blade's champion-hit mana restore let you survive Spirit Cleave poke and farm under tower, but you are not fighting him yet. At 6 Riftwalk changes everything: a blink dodges the Q3 knock-up and Fate Sealed, which is 120s at rank 1 and lands him behind the LAST champion in its line before pulling everyone in. This is the stage you climb from losing to even.

edits.before: Late is where I take over — that's why this lane is favoured for me even though it starts ugly. Once I'm 2+ items deep with Riftwalk stacking and Nashor's or Rabadon's online, my blink-spam mobility and Void Stone's 15% magic reduction let me chase him down and burst him before his E (Soul Unbound) snaps his spirit back to his body and escapes. He's a slippery duelist, but I'm slipperier — bait his E, then re-blink onto him the moment it pops. The one warning: don't get caught flat-footed by his R knock-up mid-blink, since that point-and-click lockdown is still what beats me.
edits.after: Late is where you take over — that's why this lane is favoured even though it starts ugly. Once you are 2+ items deep with Riftwalk stacking and Nashor's or Rabadon's online, blink-spam and Void Stone's 15% magic reduction let you hunt him through Soul Unbound (22s at rank 1). Treat the spirit form as a commitment rather than an escape: he is FORCED back to the body he left, so hold that ground and his exit becomes a return trip into your burst. The warning: Fate Sealed anchors on the last champion in its line and pulls you in from 1000 units.

notes: This page was written in the first person ('the worst of this lane for me', 'I save Null Sphere's shield') across early, mid and late, unlike the second-person voice used everywhere else in the champion. I converted the three strings I was already rewriting; if any other Kassadin matchups carry the same drift they should be swept together. Also worth noting for whoever tunes the winCon rows: this page asks 'is Soul Unbound down?' as the single commit question, but Soul Unbound is 22s and Fate Sealed is 120s — the ultimate is by far the more valuable thing to count, and the winCon string is outside the set of paths I rewrote here because fixing it properly means rewriting the sentence rather than patching a clause.
